proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal F_s\), a grid point \(y=y_j\), and write
\(x=R_0(y)\).  The pushforward identities are
\[
 f_{C1}(p(x))\det S(x)=f_{C0}(x),\qquad
 q(T(y))\det H(y)=f_{T1}(y),\qquad
 q(p(x))\det S(x)=f_{T0}(x).
 \tag{40}
\]
Since \(T(y)=p(x)\), \(D(y)=S(x)^{-1}H(y)\), and
\(\alpha(y)=f_{T0}(x)/f_{C0}(x)\), (40) implies
\[
 f_{C0}(x)\det D(y)=f_{C1}(T(y))\det H(y)
 =\frac{f_{T1}(y)}{\alpha(y)},
 \qquad f_{T0}(x)\det D(y)=f_{T1}(y).
 \tag{41}
\]
Every division is valid by ass:density-positivity.  In the order-minus-one
part of def:nested-derivative the two control noises have multiplier
\(\alpha(y)\), while the treated-pre and treated-post noises have
multipliers of absolute value one.  After squaring and applying (41),
their local source intensities in treated-post coordinates are,
respectively,
\[
 \alpha(y)f_{T1}(y),\quad \alpha(y)f_{T1}(y),\quad
 f_{T1}(y),\quad f_{T1}(y).
 \tag{42}
\]

By lem:uniform-critical-estimates, replacing the exact transformed scores
by their frozen-pole versions changes each cellwise covariance by
\(O(\sqrt{L_n})+1\): the exact-versus-frozen error is \(O(1)\) in
\(L^2\), while each leading score has norm \(O(\sqrt{L_n})\).  The same
lemma gives \(O(1)\) variance for the order-minus-two term.  The harmonic
score has \(O(1)\) variance by thm:nested-derivative; its covariance with
a leading score is \(O(\sqrt{L_n})\) by Cauchy--Schwarz.  Hence all these
terms vanish after division by \(L_n\), although none is deleted from the
finite-bandwidth score.

For \(B_0=B(y)\), equation (27) in
lem:uniform-critical-estimates gives the local matrix
\[
 \frac{B(y)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}L_n+O(1).
 \tag{43}
\]
Independence in ass:four-sample-design makes the four cell covariances
add, and ass:cell-ratios supplies their weights.  Combining (42)--(43)
therefore gives the \(j\)-th diagonal block
\[
 \left\{\alpha(y)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})
 +\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\right\}
 f_{T1}(y)\frac{B(y)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}.
 \tag{44}
\]
Since \(B(y)=f_{T1}(y)H(y)^{-1}\), (44) equals
\[
 V_j=\frac{\left\{\alpha(y)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})
 +\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\right\}
 \sqrt{\det H(y)}H(y)}{4\pi f_{T1}(y)}.
 \tag{45}
\]
For \(j\ne k\), lem:uniform-critical-estimates and
ass:fixed-separated-grid give only an \(O(1)\) product integral because
the two poles remain uniformly separated in every observation cell.
Thus every off-diagonal block divided by \(L_n\) tends to zero.  The
constants are uniform over \(\mathcal F_s\), so assembling the finitely
many blocks proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \lVert\Sigma_{h_n}(P)-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This calculation includes the covariance between the direct and
generated-target appearances of each control noise; independent-cell
sampling removes only cross-cell covariance and cannot cancel (45).

Let
\[
 S_n=-\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac1{n_g}
       \sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i}),
 \tag{46}
\]
where the minus sign converts the derivative of the lifted map into the
derivative of the displacement.  It has no effect on its covariance.
The four arrays in (46) are independent by ass:four-sample-design and
are centered by the definition of \(\Psi_{g,h}\).  Equation (24) of
lem:uniform-critical-estimates gives an envelope \(Ch_n^{-1}\).  Hence
each summand of \(\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\) is bounded by
\[
 \frac{C}{\sqrt{nL_n}\,h_n}=o(1),
 \tag{47}
\]
because \(n h_n^2L_n\to\infty\) under ass:polynomial-bandwidth.  The
Lindeberg condition is therefore uniform.  More quantitatively, polar
integration of the cube of (24) gives
\(\mathbb E\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)\rVert^3\leq Ch_n^{-1}\); the sum of the
third-order Taylor remainders of every scalar characteristic function is
bounded by \(C/(\sqrt n h_nL_n^{3/2})=o(1)\).  Thus, for every
\(t\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), the characteristic function of
\(t^{\mathsf T}\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\) converges uniformly once its quadratic
variance does.

Direct calculation gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\left(\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\right)
 =\frac1{L_n}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac n{n_g}
   \operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)).
 \tag{48}
\]
Ass:cell-ratios and lem:full-critical-covariance make (48) converge
uniformly to \(V(P)\).  Tightness follows from the uniform second-moment
bound.  Convolving a bounded Lipschitz test function with a centered
Gaussian of covariance \(\epsilon I_{2J}\), applying Fourier inversion,
and then sending \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) converts the preceding
characteristic-function convergence into
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}d_{\mathrm{BL}}
 \left(\mathcal L_P[\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n],N(0,V(P))\right)\to0.
 \tag{49}
\]

It remains to compare (46) with the plug-in estimator.  On the good event
of lem:uniform-critical-estimates, apply its quadratic expansion with
\(u_g=\widetilde f_g-f_g\).  Centering the stochastic KDE terms produces
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau(P)=S_n+b_n+r_n,
 \tag{50}
\]
where kernel moment cancellation gives
\(\lVert b_n\rVert\leq Ch_n^{s-2}\), and
\[
 \lVert r_n\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_g
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}\right)^2.
 \tag{51}
\]
The first and third scale conditions in lem:bandwidth-feasibility imply
\[
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\lVert b_n\rVert=o(1),\qquad
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\lVert r_n\rVert=o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \tag{52}
\]
uniformly.  By (31), the complement of the good event has probability
at most \(C\exp(-cnh_n^{13/2})=o(1)\).  Ass:lift-regularity and the
\(C^1\) map consistency in (36) show on the good event that both estimated
maps stay on the selected half-open-cell branches.  Thus the measurable
fallback occurs with probability \(o(1)\) uniformly and does not change
(49).  Equations (49)--(52), and the fact that a bounded Lipschitz
functional changes by at most the norm of its argument perturbation,
prove the asserted uniform joint Gaussian limit.  By
lem:published-critical-boundary, the comparison with the published
uniform-law, fixed-source result is strict because (42) contains four
independent source intensities, variable \(B\), and the generated target
terms.

Write
\(\widehat\Psi_{g,i}=\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})\) and
\(\Psi_{g,i}=\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i})\).  Conditional on the opposite-fold
pilots, the observations in an evaluation fold are independent of the
functions used to calculate their scores.  Lem:uniform-critical-estimates
gives
\[
 \max_{g,r}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n}),
 \quad
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\rVert^4
 =O_{\mathbb P}(h_n^{-2}).
 \tag{53}
\]
The same lemma gives \(\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_2=O(\sqrt{L_n})\).
The identity
\(aa^{\mathsf T}-bb^{\mathsf T}=(a-b)a^{\mathsf T}+b(a-b)^{\mathsf T}\)
and Cauchy--Schwarz therefore imply, conditionally on the pilots,
\[
 \frac1{L_n}\left\lVert
 \operatorname{Cov}_{P_g}(\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X))
 -\operatorname{Cov}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n}(X))
 \right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{54}
\]

For each of the finitely many matrix entries, conditional Chebyshev and
the fourth-moment bound in (53) make the centered empirical outer-product
error, after division by \(L_n\),
\[
 O_{\mathbb P}\left(\frac1{\sqrt n\,h_nL_n}\right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \tag{55}
\]
because \(nh_n^2L_n^2\to\infty\).  Replacing the conditional mean by the
fold mean adds the outer product of a fold-mean error.  Its normalized
size is \(O_{\mathbb P}(1/n)=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), using the second-moment
bound in lem:uniform-critical-estimates.  The factors \(n/n_g\) are
bounded by one and converge to \(\rho_g^{-1}\).  Summing (54)--(55) over
the four cells and two folds yields
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-\Sigma_{h_n}(P)=o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \tag{56}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).  Lem:full-critical-covariance now proves
the first covariance-consistency assertion.

Since \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^R-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+n^{-1},
\]
which proves the ridged assertion.  Finally,
\(w_j\geq\rho_{T1}^{-1}\geq\bar\rho^{-1}\),
\(\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}\geq\lambda\),
\(\lambda_{\min}(H(y_j))\geq\lambda\), and
\(f_{T1}(y_j)\leq C\).  Hence
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(V_j(P))\geq\frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi C\bar\rho}>0.
 \tag{57}
\]
On the event where the covariance error is smaller than half the right
side of (57), the resolvent identity gives
\[
 \lVert(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}-V_j(P)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R}-V_j(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
There are finitely many blocks, so the claimed uniform inverse consistency
follows.  Harmonic and generated-target scores were present throughout
(53)--(56); their normalized limiting contributions vanish only by the
bounds proved above.

Every summand defining \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\) is a nonnegative
multiple of an outer product, so \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\succeq0\).
Because \(\theta_n=n^{-1}>0\),
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^R
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}+n^{-1}I_{2J}\succ0
 \tag{58}
\]
in every sample.  Thus all principal blocks are invertible and the
nonnegative multiplier maximum has a well-defined conditional quantile.

Independence and unit variance of the Gaussian multipliers give the exact
conditional identity
\[
 Z^\star\mid\{X_{g,i}\}
 \sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}),
 \tag{59}
\]
because its conditional covariance is
\[
 \frac n{L_n}\sum_g\frac1{n_g^2}\sum_i
 (\widehat\Psi_{g,i}-\overline\Psi_{g,r(i)})
 (\widehat\Psi_{g,i}-\overline\Psi_{g,r(i)})^{\mathsf T}
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}.
\]
By thm:adjoint-covariance, both covariance matrices in (59) and in the
studentizing quadratic forms converge uniformly to \(V(P)\).  Continuity
of finite-dimensional Gaussian laws and of inversion on matrices bounded
away from singularity therefore sends the conditional multiplier maximum
to
\[
 M_P=\max_{1\leq j\leq J}Z_j^{\mathsf T}V_j(P)^{-1}Z_j,
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,V(P)).
 \tag{60}
\]
The matrix \(V(P)\) is block diagonal by its displayed definition and is
positive definite by the bound (57) proved in thm:adjoint-covariance.
Hence the standardized blocks in
(60) are independent \(N(0,I_2)\), and
\[
 \mathbb P(M_P\leq x)=(1-e^{-x/2})^J,qquad x\geq0.
 \tag{61}
\]
This law is continuous, is independent of \(P\), and has the unique
\((1-\gamma)\)-quantile
\[
 c_{1-\gamma}=-2\log\left(1-(1-\gamma)^{1/J}\right).
 \tag{62}
\]
Thus the conditional multiplier quantile converges uniformly to (62).
Thm:joint-critical-clt and thm:adjoint-covariance give the same limit
(61) for the maximum of the studentized estimation errors because matrix
inversion and the finite maximum are continuous on the uniformly
positive-definite blocks.  Comparing it with the conditional quantile proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\left\{
 \tau_j(P)\in\mathcal E_j\text{ for all }1\leq j\leq J\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\gamma.
\]

For the upper bound, use the expansion (50).  By
lem:uniform-critical-estimates and independence,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert S_n\rVert^2
 =\sup_P\sum_g\frac1{n_g}
 \mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)\rVert^2
 \leq C\frac{L_n}{n}.
 \tag{63}
\]
The bias satisfies \(\lVert b_n\rVert\leq Ch_n^{s-2}\), and
lem:bandwidth-feasibility gives \(\lVert b_n\rVert^2=o(L_n/n)\).  On the
good event, (51) and the fourth-moment estimate in
lem:uniform-critical-estimates yield
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P[\lVert r_n\rVert^2;\,\text{good event}]
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{nh_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}\right\}^2
 =o(L_n/n).
 \tag{64}
\]
For the stochastic square in (64), the ratio to \(L_n/n\) is bounded by
\(C\log n/(nh_n^9)\to0\) because \(a_h<1/9\).  The squared-bias and mixed
ratios vanish when \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\) and \(s\geq8\), exactly as in
lem:bandwidth-feasibility.

On the exceptional event the lift selector uses either a regular torus
optimal map or its fixed identity fallback.  In both cases every selected
torus displacement has a representative in the compact injectivity cell,
so \(\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2\leq C_J\).  Equation (31) gives
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P[\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2;
 \text{bad event}]
 \leq C_JC_0e^{-c_0nh_n^{13/2}}=o(L_n/n),
 \tag{65}
\]
because \(a_h<1/9<2/13\).  Combining (63)--(65) proves the class-uniform
upper risk with a constant \(C_1\).

For the lower bound, fix \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\) and
use the two alternatives from def:green-local-alternatives.  Put
\[
 \Delta_n=\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}
 \{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|,qquad
 Q_{n,\sigma}=\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}
 P_{n,\sigma,g}^{\otimes n_g}.
\]
For any estimator, choose the nearer of the two scalar values obtained by
projecting its first block on \(\upsilon\).  A testing error entails
squared vector loss at least \(\Delta_n^2/4\).  The elementary identity
for the minimum sum of two testing errors then gives
\[
 \max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_{n,\sigma}}
 \lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P_{n,\sigma})\rVert^2
 \geq\frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}
 \{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_{n,+},Q_{n,-})\}.
 \tag{66}
\]
Choose \(\zeta\) as allowed by lem:green-local-alternatives so its product
Hellinger bound is at most \(1/2\).  Since
\(\operatorname{TV}\leq\operatorname{Hel}\) under the displayed
Hellinger convention, the braces in (66) are bounded below by a positive
constant.  The same lemma gives
\[
 \Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2
 \frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}n,qquad
 \log(1/\varepsilon_n)=\eta\log n=\frac{\eta}{a_h}L_n,
 \tag{67}
\]
and places both alternatives in
\(\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))\).  The selected translations change by
only \(O(n^{-1/2})\), as proved in lem:green-local-alternatives, which is
smaller than the separation in (67) and therefore has not been discarded.
Taking the infimum over estimators in (66), multiplying by \(n/L_n\), and
taking the lower limit proves the asserted bound with
\(c_0(P_0)>0\).  Together with (63)--(65), this establishes the matched
order \(L_n/n\).

added_lemmas.statement: For a fixed sufficiently regular source law and a spatially regular \(C^1\) path of positive target densities, the corresponding optimal-transport maps form a \(C^1\) path in a H\"older topology, and the path derivative is the uniquely normalized solution of the linearized Monge--Amp\`ere equation.

source.verbatim_statement: then the curve \(\{\nabla\phi_t\}_{t\in I}\subset\mathcal C^{1,\alpha}(\overline{\Omega})\) is also \(\mathcal C^1\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 3.2; the locator contains the derivative equation and its normalization.

added_lemmas.statement: Proposition 29 of ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT supplies the two-dimensional pointwise periodized-KDE optimal-transport Gaussian conclusion in the fixed-source uniform-to-uniform case; it does not establish the general variable-coefficient or generated-target case.

attestation.note: The scope boundary was checked against the proposition and the paper's discussion of the unresolved general-coefficient critical case.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, ass:outer-ellipticity, ass:lift-regularity, ass:fixed-separated-grid, ass:kernel-symmetry, ass:kernel-mass, ass:kernel-order, ass:four-sample-design, and ass:polynomial-bandwidth, the following estimates hold uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).  For \(h=h_n\), every coordinate of the score \(\Psi_{g,h}\) is the sum of its frozen-coefficient, first-order-coordinate Green score and a remainder whose \(L^2(P_g)\) norm is bounded by a common constant.  In particular,
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C\sqrt{L_n},
 \qquad
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}\mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C h_n^{-2}.
\]
For the opposite-fold adjoint scores,
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G,\ r\in\{1,2\}}
 L_n^{-1/2}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
and, on events whose probabilities tend to one uniformly,
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C h_n^{-2}.
\]
Moreover, if \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) is a zero-integral four-density perturbation, the perturbed densities are positive, and \(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}\) is smaller than a common constant, then the selected lifted nested map in def:identified-functional obeys
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}
 \left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j
 \right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}\right)^2.
\]
For the signed periodized KDEs,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_g
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}^4\right]
 \leq C\left\{
 \frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}
 \right\}^2,
\]
and there are constants \(c_0,C_0,\epsilon_0>0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\left(
 \max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}>\epsilon_0
 \right)
 \leq C_0\exp(-c_0 n h_n^{13/2}).
\]
On the complementary good event clipping is inactive, normalization is exactly one, the selected lift branches are the population branches, all population and pilot coefficients are uniformly elliptic, and every pilot pole differs from its population pole by \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(\vartheta=1/4\).  All constants below depend only on
\(c,C,R,\lambda,\Lambda,\beta,\delta_0,J,K,s\) and the fixed upper
bound \(\bar\rho\), and hence not on \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).  We divide
the proof into six steps.

\emph{Step 1: uniform coefficient bounds and the local Green
parametrix.}  The change-of-variables equations for \(p\) and \(T\),
together with ass:density-positivity and the two ellipticity assumptions,
give uniform positive lower and upper eigenvalue bounds for \(A,B\), and
\(\mathsf C\).  Differentiating the two Monge--Amp\`ere equations and
using ass:density-smoothness gives, by induction, uniform
\(C^{s-2,\vartheta}\) bounds for these three matrices, for \(R_0,T\),
and for \(\alpha\).  To see that the constants are uniform, at each
induction step freeze the coefficient on a ball of fixed radius, absorb
the coefficient oscillation into the left side, apply the constant
coefficient estimate after an affine change of variables, and cover
\(\mathbb T^2\) by finitely many such balls.  For a mean-zero periodic
function, Parseval's identity gives
\[
 \lVert u\rVert_2^2=\sum_{k\neq0}|\widehat u(k)|^2
 \leq(4\pi^2)^{-1}\sum_{k\neq0}4\pi^2|k|^2|\widehat u(k)|^2
 =(4\pi^2)^{-1}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_2^2,
\]
which controls the normalization.  This proves, in particular, the
periodic Schauder estimate
\[
 \lVert v\rVert_{C^{k+2,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\lVert-\operatorname{div}(E\nabla v)\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}},
 \qquad \int_{\mathbb T^2}v=0,
 \tag{17}
\]
for \(E=B,\mathsf C\) and every integer \(0\leq k\leq s-4\).

Fix \(y\in\mathcal Y_J\), let \(G_B(y,z)\) be the mean-zero periodic
Green kernel of \(\mathcal L_B\), and put \(B_y=B(y)\).  The constant
coefficient fundamental solution is
\[
 \Gamma_{B_y}(z)
 =-\frac{1}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}
       \log(z^{\mathsf T}B_y^{-1}z),
 \qquad
 \nabla\Gamma_{B_y}(z)
 =-\frac{B_y^{-1}z}
 {2\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}\,z^{\mathsf T}B_y^{-1}z}.
 \tag{18}
\]
Choose a smooth cutoff equal to one in a fixed ball about zero.  Applying
\(\mathcal L_B\) to the cut-off translate of (18) leaves, away from the
Dirac mass, a divergence-form forcing whose singular part is
\[
 (B(z)-B_y)\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}(z-y),
 \qquad
 \left\lVert(B(z)-B_y)\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}(z-y)\right\rVert
 \leq C d_{\mathbb T^2}(z,y)^{-1+\vartheta}.
 \tag{19}
\]
The cutoff terms are bounded.  Solve the residual equation with zero
mean.  On a dyadic annulus of radius \(r\), rescale to a unit annulus,
apply (17) to the residual equation, and sum the geometric series
\(\sum_{m\geq0}(2^{-m}r)^{\vartheta}\).  This gives the sharper local
expansion required here,
\[
 \nabla_zG_B(y,z)=\nabla\Gamma_{B(y)}(z-y)+R_B(y,z),
 \qquad
 \lVert R_B(y,z)\rVert
 \leq C d_{\mathbb T^2}(z,y)^{-1+\vartheta}.
 \tag{20}
\]
This derivation uses the variable coefficient only through its uniform
ellipticity and \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) modulus.  Consequently its constant
is uniform over the declared class.  Notice that
\[
 \int_0^{r_0}r^{-2+2\vartheta}r\,dr<\infty.
 \tag{21}
\]
Thus the remainder in (20) is uniformly square integrable.  This is the
critical estimate not supplied by a fixed-path differentiability result.

\emph{Step 2: transformed kernels and the order-minus-two term.}
For a fixed output coordinate \(y_j\), the four leading terms in
def:nested-derivative have observation-coordinate poles
\[
 z_{C0,j}=z_{T0,j}=R_0(y_j),\qquad
 z_{C1,j}=T(y_j),\qquad z_{T1,j}=y_j.
 \tag{22}
\]
Each coordinate map in (22) is uniformly bi-Lipschitz.  In a normal
chart about its pole, write it as \(F(x)=F(z)+J_z(x-z)+E_z(x)\), where
\(\lVert E_z(x)\rVert\leq C\lVert x-z\rVert^2\).  The derivative of the
homogeneous kernel in (18) is \(O(\lVert x-z\rVert^{-2})\); hence replacing
\(F\) by its first differential changes the unsmoothed singular score by
\(O(1)\).  Convolution with the signed periodized kernel preserves this
bound in \(L^2\), because \(\lVert K_h^{\mathrm{per}}\rVert_{L^1}\) is
bounded uniformly in \(h\).  Combining this fact with (20)--(21) proves
that every exact transformed leading score differs from its frozen
coefficient, first-order-coordinate version by \(O(1)\) in
\(L^2(P_g)\), uniformly in \(g,j,P\).

For the second elliptic term of def:nested-derivative, its unsmoothed
kernel is bounded by
\[
 C\int_{\mathbb T^2}
 \frac{dz}{d_{\mathbb T^2}(y_j,z)\,d_{\mathbb T^2}(z,w)}
 \leq C\{1+|\log d_{\mathbb T^2}(y_j,w)|\}.
 \tag{23}
\]
To verify the last inequality, split the integral into the balls of
radius \(d(y_j,w)/2\) about the two poles and their complement; polar
integration handles the balls, and dyadic annuli handle the complement.
The square of the right side is integrable on \(\mathbb T^2\).  Young's
inequality therefore gives a uniform \(O(1)\) score norm after smoothing.
The coupled finite-dimensional equation determining the harmonic
translations has smooth coefficients and smooth adjoint right-hand
sides.  Estimate (17) and the branch margin in ass:lift-regularity give
a bounded score, hence bounded second and fourth moments.  This strengthens
the \(L^2\) conclusion already recorded in thm:nested-derivative without
setting either translation equal to zero.

The frozen singular score satisfies the pointwise envelope
\[
 \lVert\Psi_{g,h,j}(x)\rVert
 \leq \frac{C}{h\vee d_{\mathbb T^2}(x,z_{g,j})}
       +C\{1+|\log d_{\mathbb T^2}(x,z_{g,j})|\}.
 \tag{24}
\]
Since \(c\leq f_g\leq C\), polar integration in (24) gives
\[
 \lVert\Psi_{g,h}\rVert_2^2\leq C\log(1/h),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\lVert\Psi_{g,h}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C\left(h^{-4}h^2+\int_h^1r^{-4}r\,dr+1\right)
 \leq Ch^{-2}.
 \tag{25}
\]
All generated-target and harmonic terms have been retained in (23)--(25).

\emph{Step 3: the logarithmic part is unchanged by smoothing.}
Outside a ball of radius \(C_Kh\), symmetry and unit mass of the kernel
give, by Taylor expansion of (18),
\[
 K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}
 =\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}+O(h^2r^{-3}).
 \tag{26}
\]
The square integral of the error in (26) is bounded because
\(h^4\int_h^{r_0}r^{-5}dr=O(1)\); the inner ball also contributes
\(O(1)\) because its area is \(O(h^2)\) and the smoothed gradient is
\(O(h^{-1})\).  Thus only the middle annulus contributes a logarithm.
With \(z=B_y^{1/2}r\omega\) and
\(\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}d\omega=\pi I_2\), direct
integration gives
\[
 \int
 (K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\nabla\Gamma_{B_y})(z)
 (K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\nabla\Gamma_{B_y})(z)^{\mathsf T}dz
 =\frac{B_y^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}\log(1/h)+O(1).
 \tag{27}
\]
If \(j\ne k\), ass:fixed-separated-grid and the uniform bi-Lipschitz
bounds keep the two poles in each observation cell a fixed distance
apart.  The product of their two \(1/r\) envelopes is integrable and is
therefore \(O(1)\).  Equations (20)--(27) prove every population score
claim in the lemma.

\emph{Step 4: KDE moments and the good event.}  For an integer
\(k\in\{0,1,2\}\), differentiation of the periodized product kernel and
a \(h\)-scale net of the torus give
\[
 \mathbb P\left(
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-\mathbb E\widetilde f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}>t
 \right)
 \leq Cn^C\exp(-c n h^{2+2k+2\vartheta}t^2)
 \tag{28}
\]
for \(0<t\leq1\).  Indeed, at a net point each centered summand is
bounded and has variance at most \(Ch^{-2-2k-2\vartheta}\).  The elementary
exponential-moment calculation
\[
 \mathbb P\left(\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_i\right|>t\right)
 \leq2\exp\left\{-\frac{nt^2}{2(\sigma^2+Mt/3)}\right\}
\]
when \(|Z_i|\leq M\) and \(n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E Z_i^2\leq\sigma^2\)
follows by expanding \(\mathbb E e^{aZ_i}\), bounding the terms of order
three and higher by the geometric series in \(aM\), and optimizing over
\(a\).  Apply this bound at the net points; the next derivative controls
interpolation between them, and a union bound produces only the displayed
polynomial factor.  Taylor's formula, the vanishing
moments through order \(s-1\), and periodicity give
\[
 \lVert\mathbb E\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}
 \leq Ch^{s-k-\vartheta}.
 \tag{29}
\]
Integrating the tail in (28), adding (29), and using the four-cell union
bound yields
\[
 \mathbb E\max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}^4
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{nh^{9/2}}+h^{2s-5/2}\right\}^2.
 \tag{30}
\]
Taking \(k=2\), a fixed sufficiently small \(\epsilon_0\), and then
using (29) gives
\[
 \mathbb P\left(\max_g
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}>\epsilon_0\right)
 \leq C_0e^{-c_0nh^{13/2}}.
 \tag{31}
\]
On this event's complement, \(\widetilde f_g\geq c/2\).  Since the
periodized kernel has mass one, \(\int\widetilde f_g=1\), so clipping is
inactive, the normalizing denominator is one, and
\(\widehat f_g=\widetilde f_g\).  The unconditional Hölder moment in
(30) is deliberately stated for the smooth signed pilot: the clipped
maximum need not be differentiable on the exceptional event.  Equality
on the good event and the bounded fallback are exactly what the map and
risk arguments require.

\emph{Step 5: tame quadratic expansion and pole rate.}  The fixed-path
differentiability substrate is recorded in
lem:fixed-path-ma-linearization-source.  We now derive the stronger
uniform quadratic estimate needed for shrinking-bandwidth directions.
For two by two
matrices the exact identity
\[
 \det(M+E)=\det M+\operatorname{cof}(M):E+\det E
 \tag{32}
\]
shows that the remainder in each Monge--Amp\`ere determinant is quadratic
in the Hessian increment.  The product and composition inequalities
\[
 \lVert uv\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\lVert u\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}
        \lVert v\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}},
 \quad
 \lVert u\circ(F+v)-u\circ F-Du\circ F\,v\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\lVert u\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}
        \lVert v\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}^2
 \tag{33}
\]
follow from the fundamental theorem of calculus.  Apply (32)--(33) first
to the inner equation, next to the exact generated-density identity
\[
 q(z)=f_{C1}(z)(f_{T0}/f_{C0})(p^{-1}(z)),
 \tag{34}
\]
and finally to the outer equation.  Division in (34) is legitimate
because every density on the good event is at least \(c/2\).  Estimate
(17) absorbs the three linearized equations.  The small
\(C^{2,\vartheta}\) norm keeps every interpolating coefficient uniformly
elliptic.  This yields
\[
 \max_j\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}\right)^2.
 \tag{35}
\]
The selected translation is the cell average of the lifted displacement.
The margin \(\Delta_{\mathrm{lift}}(P)>\beta\) prevents a branch change
under the same small perturbation; integrating the map expansion proves
that its translation remainder also satisfies (35).  Thus (35) includes,
rather than deletes, the translation-aware branch derivative.

Applying the corresponding first-order Schauder stability estimate in
\(C^{0,\vartheta}\) to the two transports and (34) gives
\[
 \lVert\widehat p-p\rVert_{C^1}
 +\lVert\widehat T-T\rVert_{C^1}
 +\lVert\widehat B-B\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^{5/2}}}+h^{s-1/4}\right).
 \tag{36}
\]
Every pole in (22) is a composition of these maps, so its distance from
the pilot pole is bounded by the right side of (36).  After division by
\(h\), this becomes
\[
 O_{\mathbb P}\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^{9/2}}}+h^{s-5/4}
 \right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \tag{37}
\]
by lem:bandwidth-feasibility.  This proves the asserted
\(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) moving-pole rate.

\emph{Step 6: estimated singular scores.}  The resolvent identity
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}-\mathcal L_B^{-1}
 =\mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}
 \operatorname{div}\{(\widehat B-B)\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\}
 \tag{38}
\]
and the same dyadic calculation as in Step 1 show that changing a
coefficient or a \(C^1\) coordinate map changes a smoothed pole score by
at most its perturbation size times \(C\sqrt{\log(1/h)}\), up to a bounded
remainder.  A pole translation by distance \(d\) costs at most \(Cd/h\)
in \(L^2\), since the derivative of the smoothed \(1/r\) kernel has
\(L^2\) norm \(O(h^{-1})\).  Consequently,
\[
 \lVert\widehat U_h-U_h\rVert_2
 \leq C\left\{
 (\lVert\widehat B-B\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
  +\lVert\widehat F-F\rVert_{C^1})\sqrt{\log(1/h)}
 +\frac{d(\widehat z,z)}h+1\right\}.
 \tag{39}
\]
Equations (36)--(37) make (39) \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n})\).  The
order-minus-two and harmonic terms remain bounded by Steps 1--2.  The
pointwise envelope (24) continues to hold on the pilot event, so the
fourth-moment calculation (25) applies conditionally.  Cross-fitting
makes each opposite-fold pilot independent of the corresponding
evaluation fold.  This proves the two adjoint-score assertions and
completes the lemma.

proposed.statement: For the full scores from def:full-score-covariance, including the harmonic translation score and the covariance between the leading and generated-target responses within each control cell, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\lVert\Sigma_{h_n}(P)-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\), where \(V(P)=\operatorname{diag}(V_1,\ldots,V_J)\), \(V_j=w_j\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)/(4\pi f_{T1}(y_j))\), and \(w_j=\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})+\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\). The normalized harmonic variance and every Green--harmonic cross-covariance vanish by the uniform \(L^2\) bound in thm:nested-derivative.
proposed.justification: The proved parametrix and transformed-coordinate calculation deliver the exact four-cell critical blocks while retaining harmonic and generated-target finite-bandwidth terms.
proposed.gap: The result goes beyond the published uniform-law critical calculation by handling variable coefficients, nonlinear pullbacks, and both appearances of each control-cell noise.
proposed.consumer: The closed form is both the inferential variance and a diagnostic benchmark for the adjoint implementation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the formerly open analytic dependency by the proved uniform critical-estimate lemma while preserving the claim.

proposed.statement: Under the stated four-sample design, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\mathcal L_P[\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))],N(0,V(P)))\to0\). Uniform map consistency and ass:lift-regularity imply that the half-open-cell lift branch is selected for both \(\widehat p\) and \(\widehat T\) with probability \(1-o(1)\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\); hence the measurable fallback has probability \(o(1)\) and does not alter the limit. This strictly extends the uniform-to-uniform, fixed-source dimension-two conclusion of Proposition 29 in ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT to general variable coefficients and to the four-input nested causal functional.
proposed.justification: The uniform stochastic expansion, moving-pole rate, and Lindeberg calculation establish the full nested displacement limit at \(\sqrt{n/L_n}\).
proposed.gap: Fixed-path differentiability and the published fixed-source uniform-law theorem do not imply the shrinking-bandwidth four-input expansion proved here.
proposed.consumer: The theorem supports uncertainty quantification for prespecified smooth bivariate displacement arrows.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved moving-pole, nonlinear-remainder, and KDE estimates directly into the Gaussian-limit theorem and remove the open-question dependency.

proposed.statement: The estimator in def:adjoint-covariance retains the finite-bandwidth harmonic translation score and every generated-target cross product and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). The harmonic variance and its Green cross-covariances vanish after division by \(L_n\), but retaining them makes the finite-bandwidth covariance exact. Uniform positive definiteness of \(V(P)\), covariance consistency, and \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\) imply \(\max_{1\le j\le J}\lVert(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}-V_j(P)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so the ridge is asymptotically negligible while every block inverse exists in every sample.
proposed.justification: Normalized pilot-score stability and the \(O(h_n^{-2})\) fourth moment make the full finite-bandwidth adjoint covariance consistently estimable under cross-fitting.
proposed.gap: Existing adjoint potential results do not cover point-gradient singularities or generated targets.
proposed.consumer: The estimator supplies feasible covariance blocks while retaining control-cell and harmonic components.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the open singular-score dependency with the proved normalized score stability and fourth-moment estimates.

proposed.statement:
For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are a class-wide constant \(C_1>0\) and center-dependent constants \(c_0(P_0)>0\) and \(\kappa(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\leq C_1\frac{L_n}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{n}{L_n}
\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
\mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\geq c_0(P_0).
\]
The lower bound is witnessed by def:green-local-alternatives and lem:green-local-alternatives, for which \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\). The upper bound remains the uniform assertion over \(\mathcal F_s\).
proposed.justification: Integrated KDE tails and bounded fallback losses close the uniform upper moment bound; the established annular alternatives give the fixed-center lower bound.
proposed.gap: The theorem matches the pointwise nested critical rate in a four-law Hellinger-local experiment not covered by global one-map minimax results.
proposed.consumer: The result certifies the \(L_n/n\) squared-risk order for the specified plug-in estimator and the impossibility of uniform local improvement.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved integrated KDE tails, exceptional-event control, and quadratic remainder moment into the uniform upper-risk assertion.

prose_updates.tldr: The intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes functional now has a complete fixed-grid critical inference theory. A uniform local Green parametrix proves that every transformed exact score differs from its frozen-pole response by a bounded \(L^2\) term; moving-pole and coefficient errors are negligible at bandwidth \(h_n\), and the two-dimensional determinant identity yields a uniform quadratic nested remainder. These estimates give the full four-cell covariance, the \(\sqrt{n/L_n}\) Gaussian limit, consistent cross-fitted adjoint covariance, simultaneous multiplier ellipses, and matching squared risk \(L_n/n\).

project_justification.gap: Published transport central-limit results do not prove pointwise gradient inference in dimension two for general variable coefficients with a generated target, and fixed-path differentiability does not control shrinking-bandwidth empirical directions. The note closes this gap by deriving the local variable-coefficient Green expansion, transformed-kernel and moving-pole stability, and a uniform nonlinear moment bound.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, each independent cell contributes a positive logarithmic Green variance. Nesting makes both control cells enter directly and through the generated target; the exact pulled-coordinate calculation retains those within-cell cross terms while showing that the remaining composition gains one derivative.
project_justification.fill: The note establishes intrinsic torus identification, the translation-aware nested derivative, an explicit four-cell covariance, a feasible cross-fitted adjoint estimator, fixed-grid multiplier ellipses, and a matched class-uniform upper and fixed-center Hellinger-local lower risk bound. The analytic closure uses a frozen-pole parametrix with an \(O(r^{-1+1/4})\) remainder, second-order coordinate changes, KDE Hölder tails, and the exact two-dimensional determinant identity.

prose_updates.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC supplies the multivariate changes-in-changes motivation and Card--Krueger application but stops short of the critical limit law proved here. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the dimension-two uniform-law fixed-source case; its general-coefficient freezing bound does not yield the present result. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supplies fixed smooth-path differentiability, whereas this note derives shrinking-bandwidth transformed-kernel, moving-pole, and quadratic nested control. GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT treats smoother potential functionals and excludes pointwise gradients. HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin address global one-map risk; the present annular Green alternatives and four-input upper bound establish a distinct fixed-center pointwise logarithmic experiment. PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand concerns one-dimensional quantile-map bands rather than fixed-grid bivariate nested ellipses.
prose_updates.interpretation: At each prespecified treated-post location \(y_j\), the estimand is the translation-aware no-treatment displacement \(y_j-T(y_j)\). The covariance weight \(\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})+\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\) shows how uncertainty from all four repeated-cross-section cells contributes. The simultaneous ellipses preserve the direction and covariance of each bivariate arrow while controlling multiplicity across the fixed grid.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The result is fixed-grid and assumes four independent smooth samples on the flat torus, uniform density positivity, uniform Brenier ellipticity, a fixed lift/cut-locus margin, and the stated polynomial bandwidth window. Numerical Monge--Ampere and adjoint solves must approximate map evaluations, coefficients, and score covariances below their respective statistical scales. The proposed nonseparable \(h,h/2,h/4,h/8\) calculation remains a valuable implementation diagnostic, but is no longer a logical premise of the proof.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved theorem concerns a balanced four-cell repeated-cross-section experiment with fixed \(J\), smooth positive periodic densities, and translation-aware torus displacements. It does not give a confidence band over \(\mathbb T^2\), allow vanishing densities or degenerating Jacobians, or justify applying the procedure directly to raw discrete or paired Card--Krueger outcomes. A Card--Krueger reanalysis therefore requires a prespecified smooth bivariate periodic outcome construction and a defensible independent-cell sampling approximation, plus numerical tolerances below the stated critical scales.
